prompt.text:
Continue from the still. the Explorer in an ivory industrial helmet with an opaque black full-face visor and cyan side-light rings, orange technical coveralls, chest instrument and grey boots stands in a foam city of pale golden bubbles held in a translucent gluten network, first tiny bubbles forming, cyan accent light. Photoreal cinematic scientific visualization, warm polished home realism, ivory-and-orange equipment palette, cyan accent light. Low motion.

At the opening of the shot, Tiny bubbles swell slowly. Ambient (slow, subtle): bubble walls shimmer and the net flexes.

Then, The Explorer turns toward camera, head raised, and says over helmet radio in a calm adult male English voice: "Something is breathing down here, Control." His mouth returns to rest.

Then, The Explorer holds still, head tilted, while Control answers in a calm adult English voice: "Yeast. It feeds on sugars in the flour and breathes out carbon dioxide. Each breath becomes a bubble, and your net from the last step is what catches them all. That is our engine." The Explorer stays in place, mouth closed.

Finally, The camera begins a slow dolly in. The camera ends on the yeast bubbles swelling in the net. Acoustic environment: faint bubbling and dough creaks; clear close dialogue front and center. The Explorer stays in frame, mouth closed.

Reference lock: continue directly from the supplied still/reference image; it is the authoritative first frame and starting composition. Preserve the exact character identities, character count, wardrobes, set layout, lighting, and every visible prop's physical size, shape, placement, and attachment. Animate only the character actions explicitly requested in the scene direction. Keep all unattended characters, props, and background elements stationary within the scene. Follow the camera movement explicitly requested in the scene direction; if none is requested, keep the camera locked to the reference framing. Directed camera motion may change framing, perspective, screen positions, apparent size, and visibility without physically moving or changing the scene's objects. Do not introduce, duplicate, physically remove, relocate, reshape, or float any character or prop.
